choices.why: A light grey, clean-lined three-seat sofa, 234 cm wide, that fills the long left wall well and keeps the room bright.
At 200x300 cm and in a soft neutral flatweave, it is big enough to define the seating area from the sofa to the TV stand without crowding the light floor.
The only truly light-wood coffee table, and its simple Scandinavian lines suit a modern living room for having friends over.
A long, low console in light cream with open shelves that keeps the space bright and modern across from the sofa.
The arc lamp reaches over the sofa from the corner by the balcony, and its black finish echoes the black window frame.
The terracotta cushions with tassels add the color the user asked for against the grey sofa and neutral tones.
A tall, airy areca palm that fills the spot by the balcony door with green and makes the most of the light.
A pair of white sheer curtains that softens the sliding door without blocking the natural light.

answer.why: Light neutrals (grey sofa, beige rug, light wood and cream furniture, white sheers) keep the living room bright and modern, while black accents echo the window frame and the terracotta cushions and palm bring warmth and color.
